scope: Breakend replacement syntax, mate/partner relationships, inserted sequence/contig examples, telomeres, event/uncertainty and single-breakend examples corresponding to VCFv4.5 tables VCF5.25-VCF5.41.

transitions.finding: The normalized non-empty breakend section lines are identical in the reviewed section ranges. The separate ALT '*' allele addition in VCFv4.2 is recorded in the genotype/SV crosswalk and is not a breakend syntax change.

The source prose is restructured and split into smaller source lines/paragraphs; the core two-breakend/one-record-per-breakend replacement syntax, four bracket orientations, mate coordinate and partner/telomere concepts are retained. This is a section-level finding; exact line-by-line requirement comparison remains part of the full source audit.

VCFv4.4 change log disallows BND ALT records and says to use breakpoint notation; this does not disallow the breakend replacement ALT syntax itself. SVTYPE is deprecated, so the earlier SVTYPE=BND tag is no longer used in the updated examples. Breakend replacement notation, mate IDs and partner semantics remain.
controls: Do not interpret 'Disallowed BND ALT records' as prohibiting breakend replacement strings; the note directs to breakpoint notation.
Distinguish the symbolic ALT allele <BND> from breakend replacement notation using bracketed mate coordinates.

transitions.finding: The breakend replacement syntax, mate/partner distinction, contig insertion, multiple mates, telomeres, EVENT and single-breakend concepts are retained. The VCFv4.5 examples reflect END deprecation/computed semantics, positive SVLEN/INV support and SVCLAIM semantics; the breakend section itself has no new bracket-orientation rule identified in this comparison.

rules: one VCF record for each breakend of a novel adjacency
REF is the sequence beginning at POS
ALT replacement contains replacement sequence, mate coordinate and orientation
four bracket arrangements encode orientation
inserted sequence may be embedded in ALT
large inserted sequence may use assembly contig
complete contig insertion shorthand is recommended
partial contig intervals and circular adjacency are represented
multiple mates are alternate alleles
partner is distinct from mate
each breakend has one partner
PARID can explicitly identify partner
virtual telomeric partners are at coordinates 0 and N+1
EVENT groups related adjacencies
symbolic inversion shorthand and explicit breakends are alternatives
microhomology uncertainty uses leftmost placement and CIPOS
MATEID and PARID preserve different relations
single breakend has no mate
unobserved partner may be represented
examples of copy-number contexts and partial insertions are illustrative, not universal obligations

table_groups.context: Basic breakend syntax and inserted sequence

related_deltas.svtype: VCFv4.4 deprecates SVTYPE; VCFv4.5 explains redundancy with ALT. See VCFv4.4.tex:2583-2590 and VCFv4.5.tex:871-877.
related_deltas.end_svlen: VCFv4.5 deprecates END, defines computed compatibility semantics and updates examples to SVLEN/FORMAT LEN. See VCFv4.5.tex:867-894.
related_deltas.svclaim: VCFv4.4 introduces SVCLAIM and claim semantics; VCFv4.5 retains. See VCFv4.4.tex:853-860; 4.5.tex:1024-1066.
